edges.description: Reduced PRDM16 dose removes its transcriptional activation of compact-myocardial genes and repression of trabecular-myocardial genes in left ventricular cardiomyocytes.
edges.target: Loss of Compact Myocardium Transcriptional Identity

edges.description: Independent of the compact-myocardium transcriptional program, monoallelic Prdm16 loss produces early, sex-modified metabolic and oxidative-stress changes in cardiac tissue.
Loss of PRDM16-mediated repression of TGF-beta pathway genes, including direct repression of the TGFB3 promoter, de-represses TGF-beta receptor signaling in cardiomyocytes.
edges.source: Loss of Compact Myocardium Transcriptional Identity

edges.description: Loss of the compact-myocardial gene program directly impairs the structural maturation of the compact ventricular wall.
edges.source: Loss of Compact Myocardium Transcriptional Identity

edges.description: Loss of PRDM16-mediated suppression of conduction-system and atrial-fate master regulators allows ectopic conduction-system tissue to expand within the ventricular myocardium.
edges.source: Loss of Compact Myocardium Transcriptional Identity
edges.target: Ventricular Conduction System Hyperplasia and Atrial-Fate Derepression

edges.description: Increased TGF-beta receptor signaling suppresses the proliferative expansion of developing left ventricular cardiomyocytes.
Oxidative stress and dysregulated cardiac energetics contribute to diminished systolic performance independently of the compaction/TGF-beta axis.
edges.target: Left Ventricular Dilation and Systolic Dysfunction

edges.description: Reduced cardiomyocyte proliferation in the developing compact myocardium limits the thickening and maturation of the compact ventricular wall.
Reduced cardiomyocyte number and thinner compact/interventricular septal myocardium predispose to progressive ventricular dilation and contractile dysfunction.
edges.target: Left Ventricular Dilation and Systolic Dysfunction

edges.description: The structurally abnormal, thinned compact wall is predisposed to progressive dilation and reduced contractile function.
edges.target: Left Ventricular Dilation and Systolic Dysfunction

edges.description: Ectopic/hyperplastic conduction-system tissue provides a structural substrate for accessory-pathway-type pre-excitation and other rhythm disturbances.
edges.source: Ventricular Conduction System Hyperplasia and Atrial-Fate Derepression

edges.description: Progressive ventricular dilation and systolic dysfunction lead to symptomatic heart failure.
edges.source: Left Ventricular Dilation and Systolic Dysfunction

edges.description: Blood stasis in a dilated, hypokinetic, structurally abnormal ventricle predisposes to intracardiac thrombus formation and embolism.
edges.source: Left Ventricular Dilation and Systolic Dysfunction

edges.description: Ventricular dilation and remodeling independently increase arrhythmogenic risk, in addition to the conduction-system substrate described above.
edges.source: Left Ventricular Dilation and Systolic Dysfunction

edges.description: Cardiomyocytes carrying the patient's own variant show a significant proliferative deficit with increased apoptosis, in human cells.
edges.limitations: hiPSC-cardiomyocytes are fetal-like and proliferation-competent, unlike adult human cardiomyocytes, so the deficit is measured against a developmental baseline that has no adult counterpart. The system is also derived from a single proband, so genetic background is not controlled.

edges.description: PRDM16 was raised and lowered in this line and its binding at the TGFB3 promoter assayed directly, establishing the repression step this node asserts.
edges.limitations: A rat immortalized cardiomyoblast line is neither human nor a cardiomyocyte, carries no LVNC8 variant, and expresses PRDM16 from an adenoviral construct rather than at endogenous dose. It establishes that PRDM16 can repress TGFB3, not that this repression sets the direction of TGF-beta signaling in patient myocardium; the conflicting in vivo directions recorded elsewhere in this entry are exactly why that distinction matters.
edges.source: H9c2 rat cardiomyoblast PRDM16 promoter-binding system

edges.description: Single-cell and spatial transcriptomics in this model define the compact-to-trabecular identity shift that the node asserts, and ChIP sequencing identifies the direct PRDM16 targets responsible.
edges.limitations: Cardiomyocyte-restricted deletion removes Prdm16 from every cardiomyocyte, whereas human LVNC8 is a germline heterozygous state with residual PRDM16 dose in all lineages, so the transcriptional shift is expected to be more complete here than in patients.
edges.target: Loss of Compact Myocardium Transcriptional Identity

edges.description: The model develops biventricular noncompaction, the structural lesion this node names.
edges.limitations: Noncompaction here is biventricular, whereas the human disease label and the patient phenotype foreground the left ventricle; the chamber distribution is therefore broader in the model than in patients.

edges.description: The model reproduces the left-ventricle-selective dilation and systolic dysfunction that distinguishes this disease from a generic cardiomyopathy, and was generated specifically because earlier conditional lines did not.
edges.limitations: Chamber selectivity is reproduced, and the paper offers the LV-restricted transcriptional program as its explanation, but presents that as an explanation for a subset of LVNC cardiomyopathies rather than a general one. How far it extends to PRDM16 patients specifically is untested.
edges.target: Left Ventricular Dilation and Systolic Dysfunction

edges.description: Homozygous Q187X animals fail to develop a normal compact myocardium, tying the human nonsense allele directly to the compaction defect.
edges.limitations: The compaction phenotype requires the homozygous state, which is embryonically lethal and has no human counterpart: LVNC8 patients are heterozygous. The allele's compaction effect in mice is therefore demonstrated at a dose humans never carry.

edges.description: Heterozygotes do show TGF-beta dysregulation, but in the opposite direction from this node: TGF-beta expression falls with age, where losing a repressor of TGFB3 predicts, and the node asserts, an increase.
edges.limitations: This is a direction mismatch on the node's asserted quantity rather than a missing measurement, which is why the link is FAILS_TO_RECAPITULATE and not PARTIALLY_RECAPITULATES: the model moves the opposite way. It also conflicts with the cardiac-specific Prdm16 null model below, where TGF-beta signaling is activated, and with the patient-derived iPSC-cardiomyocytes, whose proliferative deficit is attributed to TGF-beta activation. Allele class, dose, Cre driver and age at measurement all differ across these systems. This paper's own proposal is that PRDM16 regulates TGF-beta bidirectionally in a temporally-dependent manner, which would reconcile them; until that is tested across models this link must not be used to infer the direction of the TGF-beta change in patients at any given stage. See discussion gap_lvnc8_tgfbeta_direction_conflict.

edges.description: The genotype-matched heterozygote develops heightened myocardial fibrosis, the one component of the human phenotype this model reproduces cleanly.
edges.limitations: Fibrosis is reported qualitatively as heightened, without a quantitative collagen measure, and no human myocardial fibrosis data exist for PRDM16 carriers to compare against.

edges.description: The heterozygous state matching the human genotype produces smaller ventricular dimensions, the opposite of the ventricular dilation seen in patients carrying this class of variant.
edges.limitations: This is a substantive negative result, not a gap in phenotyping: the heterozygous Q187X mouse is the genotype-matched animal and it diverges in direction from the human phenotype on this node. Ventricular dimensions from this model must not be used to infer human chamber remodeling, and any therapeutic inference about reverse remodeling drawn from it would be inverted. Fibrosis is reproduced, so the model remains informative for the fibrotic component while failing on chamber size.
edges.target: Left Ventricular Dilation and Systolic Dysfunction

edges.description: Metabolomic profiling of cardiac tissue defines the substrate-utilization and oxidative-stress changes this node asserts, at the earliest detectable stage.
edges.limitations: The metabolic phenotype is sex-dimorphic in this model and no equivalent human cardiac metabolomic data exist for PRDM16 carriers, so neither the magnitude nor the sex dependence has been confirmed in patients.

edges.description: Systolic performance is reduced, matching the human phenotype, but the hearts are hypoplastic rather than dilated.
edges.limitations: Only the systolic-dysfunction half of this node is reproduced. Chamber geometry moves the wrong way: hypoplastic hearts are not dilated hearts, the same divergence the Q187X heterozygote shows. Both monoallelic mouse models therefore fail on the dilation component, which is worth weighing before treating either as a model of the remodeling process.
edges.target: Left Ventricular Dilation and Systolic Dysfunction

edges.description: Developmental myocardial Prdm16 loss expands the distal ventricular conduction system, the structural change this node asserts.
edges.limitations: The Sm22alpha-Cre driver is not cardiomyocyte-exclusive: the authors report that it also eliminates PRDM16 in smooth muscle cells, and argue the cardiomyocyte loss is the primary culprit on the grounds that smooth muscle coverage was unaffected. Deletion is also developmental, where patients carry partial lifelong haploinsufficiency; whether that produces conduction-system expansion of comparable extent has not been shown, and no human histological counterpart is available.
edges.target: Ventricular Conduction System Hyperplasia and Atrial-Fate Derepression

edges.description: The model develops abnormal postnatal electrophysiology and premature death, giving an in vivo arrhythmic phenotype downstream of the conduction-system expansion.
edges.limitations: The model reports abnormal electrophysiology and premature death, not ventricular pre-excitation specifically. The accessory-pathway phenotype that names this node is documented in a human PRDM16 carrier and has no demonstrated counterpart in this mouse, so the model supports the arrhythmia half of the node and not the pre-excitation half.

edges.description: Reduced prdm16 dose and a human truncation allele both impair cardiomyocyte proliferative capacity, the claim this node makes.
edges.limitations: Zebrafish cardiomyocytes retain proliferative and regenerative capacity that mammalian cardiomyocytes lose after birth, so the baseline biology of the readout differs from the human one. The zebrafish heart is also two-chambered and has no compact-versus-trabecular left ventricular architecture, so this model cannot address the chamber-specific arm of the mechanism at all.
edges.source: Zebrafish prdm16 haploinsufficiency and truncation model

edges.description: Contractile dysfunction is reproduced; ventricular dilation is not assessable in this organism.
edges.limitations: The zebrafish heart has a single ventricle with no left-ventricular counterpart, so the chamber-specific dilation this node names cannot be observed here. Only the contractile-dysfunction component transfers, and the partial cardiomyocyte uncoupling reported alongside it has no established human correlate in LVNC8.
edges.source: Zebrafish prdm16 haploinsufficiency and truncation model
edges.target: Left Ventricular Dilation and Systolic Dysfunction

edges.description: TGF-beta signaling is activated in Prdm16-null hearts at both ligand transcript and downstream effector level, the direction predicted by PRDM16 acting as a repressor of TGFB transcription.
edges.limitations: This model's direction conflicts with the Prdm16Q187X heterozygote, which shows age-dependent loss of TGF-beta expression. The two differ in allele class (complete cardiac null versus a heterozygous nonsense variant), dose and timepoint. The Q187X paper proposes that PRDM16 regulates TGF-beta bidirectionally in a temporally-dependent manner, which would make the two findings phases of one mechanism; that has not been tested across models, so the sign of the TGF-beta change in human LVNC8 should not be inferred from either model alone. The driver is alpha-MHC (Myh6)-Cre, attributed by PMID:37395136 rather than stated in this paper's own record here, and it matters: Myh6-Cre knockouts are reported to give hypertrophy in one model and LV dilation in another, and a later paper judged the earlier conditional Prdm16 lines not to mirror the patient LVNC phenotype.
edges.source: Cardiac-specific Prdm16 conditional knockout mouse (conduction and fibrosis phenotype)

edges.description: Prdm16-null hearts develop increased fibrosis with cardiomyocyte hypertrophy, quantified by trichrome staining, densitometry and hydroxyproline assay and accompanied by upregulated extracellular-matrix and myofibroblast transcripts.
edges.limitations: Fibrosis here is measured in a complete cardiac null; patients are heterozygous, and no quantitative human myocardial fibrosis data exist for PRDM16 carriers to calibrate the magnitude against.
edges.source: Cardiac-specific Prdm16 conditional knockout mouse (conduction and fibrosis phenotype)

edges.description: Prdm16-null hearts show measurable conduction and repolarization abnormalities (prolonged QRS and QTc) alongside dysregulated ion channel transcripts, giving a TGF-beta-independent substrate for the arrhythmia node.
edges.limitations: The phenotype is conduction slowing and repolarization prolongation, not the accessory-pathway pre-excitation that names this node; no pre-excitation is reported in this model. Blocking the TGF-beta receptor does not reverse the conduction abnormality, so the arrhythmic substrate here is not downstream of the TGF-beta arm and should not be treated as such.
edges.source: Cardiac-specific Prdm16 conditional knockout mouse (conduction and fibrosis phenotype)

edges.description: Fibrosis develops with an incidence and severity that differ by sex, assessed by histology and qPCR at 7 months.
edges.limitations: The sex dependence of the fibrotic response has no confirmed human counterpart, and the model is a cardiac-restricted null against germline heterozygosity in patients.
edges.source: Sex-stratified cardiac-specific Prdm16 conditional knockout mouse

edges.description: Contractile dysfunction and fibrosis develop with an incidence and severity that differ by sex, more severe in females, and female animals carry significantly elevated mortality.
edges.limitations: The reported outcome is contractile dysfunction with fibrosis rather than chamber dilation specifically, so this link covers the systolic-failure half of the node. The model is a cardiac-restricted null, whereas LVNC8 patients are germline heterozygotes, and the human comparison in the same paper is a contiguous-gene-deletion cohort rather than nonsyndromic PRDM16 variant carriers.
edges.source: Sex-stratified cardiac-specific Prdm16 conditional knockout mouse
edges.target: Left Ventricular Dilation and Systolic Dysfunction

nodes.description: PRDM16-associated cardiomyopathy carries an increased risk of cardiac arrhythmia. Beyond the remodeling-driven arrhythmia risk shared with other dilated/noncompaction cardiomyopathies, one reported adolescent carrier presented with Wolff-Parkinson-White syndrome (ventricular pre-excitation via a complex accessory pathway), mechanistically consistent with the conduction-system-hyperplasia node above.

evidence.reference_title: A rare genetic variant in PRDM16 is associated with Wolff-Parkinson-White syndrome with complex accessory pathway characteristics and left ventricular non-compaction cardiomyopathy.

evidence.snippet: The incidence rates of all-cause mortality, stroke and systemic emboli, heart failure admission, cardiac transplantation, ventricular arrhythmias, and cardiac device implantation were 2.16, 1.54, 3.53, 1.24, 2.17, and 2.66, respectively, per 100 person-years.

nodes.description: Independently of the compact-myocardium transcriptional program, monoallelic Prdm16 loss produces early metabolic dysregulation in cardiac tissue: reduced amino-acid, glycerol, glycolytic, and tricarboxylic-acid-cycle metabolites, diminished glutathione with increased inosine monophosphate (indicating oxidative stress and dysregulated energetics), and up-regulation of two novel candidate cardiac metabolic regulators, PYROXD2 and PBXIP1. The phenotype is sex-modified: cardiac dysfunction and reduced glucose utilization are more pronounced in female mice, while triacylglyceride accumulation and reduced fatty-acid utilization are male-specific.

evidence.snippet: Prdm16csp1/wt mice are viable up to 8 months, develop hypoplastic hearts, and diminished systolic performance that is more pronounced in female mice.

evidence.reference_title: Prdm16 mutation determines sex-specific cardiac metabolism and identifies two novel cardiac metabolic regulators.

evidence.reference_title: Prdm16 mutation determines sex-specific cardiac metabolism and identifies two novel cardiac metabolic regulators.

nodes.description: Cardiac-restricted Prdm16 null model phenotyped by electrocardiography, fibrosis histology and left ventricular RNA sequencing. It is the only model in this entry that measures TGF-beta pathway activity in vivo and then tests it pharmacologically: TGF-beta signaling is activated in Prdm16-null hearts, but blocking the TGF-beta receptor does not rescue the conduction defect. That negative rescue result separates the fibrotic and conduction arms of the mechanism, and the accompanying ion-channel transcript dysregulation offers a TGF-beta-independent route to the arrhythmia node.

nodes.description: Loss of PRDM16-driven compact myocardial specification and reduced compact-layer cardiomyocyte proliferation leave a thick, spongy trabeculated layer with deep intertrabecular recesses overlying a thinned compacted wall, predominantly affecting the left ventricle. In cardiomyocyte-specific Prdm16 knockout mice this produces biventricular noncompaction with LV-specific thinning of the compact myocardium and interventricular septum detectable from embryonic day 15.5.

nodes.description: PRDM16 is a compact-myocardium-enriched transcription factor that activates a compact-myocardial gene program while repressing a trabecular-myocardial gene program, in part through cooperation with the LV-enriched transcription factors TBX5 and HAND1. In cardiomyocyte-specific Prdm16 knockout mice, compact myocardial cardiomyocytes shift from a compact transcriptional identity toward one resembling trabecular myocardium or neurons, with reduced cardiomyocyte proliferation localized to the left ventricular compact layer and interventricular septum. Independently, single-cell RNA+ATAC sequencing shows PRDM16 favors ventricular working cardiomyocyte identity specifically by opposing the master regulators of ventricular conduction and atrial fate, so its loss also derepresses a conduction-system/atrial transcriptional program.

nodes.description: Heterozygous truncating (nonsense, frameshift) or missense PRDM16 variants reduce the dose or activity of the PRDM16 zinc-finger transcription factor. Variants cluster across the gene's 17 exons and were first mapped within the terminal 1p36 deletion syndrome critical region before being confirmed as an independent cause of nonsyndromic disease. A contemporary review reports a variant-class correlation: missense variants track with DCM, while nonsense and frameshift (loss-of-function) variants track with LVNC, and PRDM16 is predicted to be highly intolerant of loss-of-function variation.

nodes.description: An independently generated cardiomyocyte-specific Prdm16 deletion, analysed by combined single-cell RNA and ATAC sequencing. It is kept separate from the Prdm16cKO model above because it interrogates a different arm of the mechanism: rather than the compact-versus-trabecular axis, it establishes that PRDM16 suppresses conduction-system and atrial fates, and that its loss expands the distal ventricular conduction system. This is the only in vivo source for the conduction and arrhythmia arm of this entry.

nodes.description: Conditional deletion of Prdm16 restricted to cardiomyocytes. Unlike earlier conditional Prdm16 lines, this model reproduces the left-ventricle-selective vulnerability seen in patients: it develops LV-specific dilation and systolic dysfunction together with biventricular noncompaction. Paired RNA sequencing, ChIP sequencing, single-cell RNA sequencing and spatial transcriptomics in the same model identify the direct transcriptional targets of PRDM16 and show that compact-layer cardiomyocytes lose their normal transcriptomic identity. It is the reference in vivo model for the compact-myocardium transcriptional arm of the LVNC8 mechanism.

nodes.description: CRISPR-mediated knock-in of the patient-derived Q187X nonsense allele, generated alongside iPSC-cardiomyocytes from the proband carrying the same variant. It is the only mouse in this entry built on a specific human LVNC8 allele rather than on gene deletion (the zebrafish model also expresses a human truncation allele), which makes it the strongest available mammalian test of allele-level causality. Homozygotes are embryonically lethal with an underdeveloped compact myocardium; heterozygotes show fibrosis and age-dependent loss of TGF-beta expression, but smaller rather than dilated ventricles.

evidence.snippet: CRISPR (clustered regularly interspaced short palindromic repeats)-mediated knock-in mouse model hosting the Prdm16Q187X allele was generated and subjected to ECG, histological, and transcriptional analysis.

nodes.description: Systemic heterozygous Prdm16 inactivation, the closest genotype match in this entry to the human heterozygous state. Profiled by transcriptomics, proteomics and metabolomics in both sexes to capture the earliest pathological window rather than end-stage disease. It is the source of the metabolic arm of the LVNC8 mechanism and of the sex-dimorphism observation: female animals are more severely affected.

evidence.reference_title: Prdm16 mutation determines sex-specific cardiac metabolism and identifies two novel cardiac metabolic regulators.
evidence.snippet: This study performed in-depth pathophysiological and molecular analyses of male and female Prdm16csp1/wt mice that carry systemic, monoallelic Prdm16 gene inactivation.

nodes.description: A cardiac-specific Prdm16 knockout generated as the animal arm of a multi-institutional 1p36 deletion cohort study and analysed by sex, with echocardiography at 4 and 6 to 7 months and fibrosis histology at 7 months. Its value is that the sex effect it reports is paired with human data in the same paper, making it the one place in this entry where a model-derived observation is tested against patients rather than only asserted.

nodes.description: PRDM16 normally binds the TGFB3 promoter and represses its transcription. Loss of PRDM16 releases this repression, producing increased TGF-beta receptor signaling in cardiomyocytes. Because TGF-beta signaling has an antiproliferative effect on cardiomyocytes, its dysregulated increase reduces cardiomyocyte proliferative capacity during the developmental window when compaction normally occurs. The INCREASED modifier records the majority position, supported by the promoter-repression mechanism, by patient-derived iPSC-cardiomyocytes, and by TGF-beta activation in Prdm16-null hearts. It is not unanimous: the genotype-matched heterozygous Prdm16Q187X mouse instead loses TGF-beta expression with age, and that model is linked below as FAILS_TO_RECAPITULATE this node. The unresolved sign is tracked in discussion gap_lvnc8_tgfbeta_direction_conflict and matters because TGF-beta inhibition is the one mechanistically motivated therapeutic direction this entry identifies.

nodes.description: PRDM16 loss removes its suppression of master regulators of ventricular conduction and atrial cell fate within ventricular working cardiomyocytes. In cardiomyocyte-specific Prdm16-deletion mice this produces hyperplasia of the distal ventricular conduction system and abnormal postnatal electrophysiology, providing a mechanistic node upstream of arrhythmia and pre-excitation phenotypes that is distinct from (and additional to) arrhythmia risk driven by ventricular dilation and remodeling.

nodes.description: The original functional model accompanying the discovery that PRDM16 mutation causes the cardiomyopathy of 1p36 deletion syndrome and a share of nonsyndromic LVNC and DCM. Both reduced prdm16 dose and a human truncation allele were modeled, producing contractile dysfunction, partial cardiomyocyte uncoupling, and impaired cardiomyocyte proliferative capacity. It is the earliest evidence tying the proliferative arm of this mechanism to the human genotype.
